sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Repair the remaining owner/type and shape-link errors before freezing. In SupportingStructureShape, replace sh:class nltl:frameAttachment with the canonical class nltl:frameAttachmentRecord; frameAttachment is an ObjectProperty, not a class. Link FrameShape's nltl:hasFrameAttachment property to FrameAttachmentRecordShape with sh:node (and enforce the record class, e.g. sh:class nltl:frameAttachmentRecord), otherwise the attachment-record constraints are never applied through the target frame. sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair the longitudinal-frame SPARQL constraint: its outer FILTER NOT EXISTS is inverted, so a compliant attachment with a bracket is reported as a violation while a missing bracket can pass. Express a violation when any longitudinal supporting web frame or bulkhead lacks a linked attachment with hasConnectionBracket. Also encode the declared relationship term hasSupportingStructureAttachment on its authoritative supportingStructure owner (or add the corresponding owner-correct inverse path); it is currently omitted and replaced only by hasAttachedSupportingStructure, despite being a required direct-constraint term. Preserve the existing within-ice applicability and all other owner-correct checks.

Repair the frame-attachment node shape: nltl:frameAttachment is an ObjectProperty, not a class, and must not be used as the sh:class target. Use the canonical class nltl:frameAttachmentRecord, matching the range of hasFrameAttachment. Keep the owner-correct hasSupportingStructureAttachment path on supportingStructure and preserve the existing applicability, relationship, conditional attachment, side-connection, and bracket-thickness/stiffening checks.

Repair applicability and ownership before freezing. Do not place nltl:effectiveAttachmentConfirmed directly on the target frame; its authoritative owner is the frameAttachment record, so constrain it through the frame-to-frameAttachment path. Gate all TRF-049 obligations by withinIceStrengthenedArea=true; the current node shape unconditionally requires attachment, thickness, and related data on frames outside the ice-strengthened area. Make the universal attachment queries pair the target frame's nltl:hasFrameAttachment record with the supporting structure's nltl:hasSupportingStructureAttachment record (and retain hasAttachedSupportingStructure, effectiveAttachmentConfirmed, and the required bracket relationship), otherwise an unrelated compliant attachment can satisfy the rule. The transverse alternative must likewise require a linked attachment record and must not let a missing record pass through FILTER NOT EXISTS. Do not make bracket thickness and stiffening conjunctively mandatory for every frame: they apply only when a bracket is installed, while the transverse rule permits either a bracket or similar construction. Preserve the owner-correct hasSupportingStructureAttachment relationship and the existing side-connection and thickness comparison checks, with the latter evaluated only for installed brackets.
